restrictions: Ordinary-collision claim on the complete digest; no witness pair is provided.
Score is an upper bound on total work in collision-frontier-v5 units, not a measured run.
Success probability 0.39 relies on premise H1 (random-mapping model) declared in proof.md section 10.
Generic birthday search only: no use of 3-round structure, no differential.
The charged point count includes the drain of all 256 lanes to distinguished points; every charged point lies on a stored trail.

heuristics.statement: For uniformly random seeds on the fixed 3-round chain F, trails merge like independent random paths and distinguished points are independent events on 2^256 points: no exploitable collision or cycle structure.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target blake3-r3-prefix-v1 with prefix K = 0^32 and the 256-bit seed of one attempt; only the merge statistics of the walk are used.
heuristics.extrapolation: Success probability and Q follow the random-mapping law at the charged point count; no width-256 test is possible, and the program controls do not test this premise.
heuristics.limitations: Declared, not proved. A merge-rate deficit eps costs 0.5*log2(1/(1-eps)) extra bits; the 0.0015 margin of proof section 6.2 covers only the losses itemised there, not a merge-rate deficit.

heuristics.statement: The emitted straight-line program is executed on 256-bit plane registers with the prices of proof.md section 3: 1 per Boolean plane gate, 0 for rotations and moves, 154-gate two-addend adders, SSA with no spills, 4-byte gate records.
heuristics.scope: The main loop of the search; the drain, the DP handlers, recovery and start generation are charged as separate rows.
heuristics.extrapolation: Gate counts are read from the emitted instruction list, so the bound scales with the program that would run; no measurement of a real machine is claimed.
heuristics.limitations: A register file smaller than about 40 planes would force spills and raise the bound. The circuit is not claimed minimal.
